title: Charge-6e superconductivity from doping SU(3) spin liquids
authors: Yan-Qi Wang, Boran Zhou, Hui Yang, Zhi-Qiang Gao
abstract: We propose doping $SU(3)$-symmetric spin liquids as a route toward charge-$6e$ superconductivity. This generalizes the idea of constructing charge-$4e$ superconductivity from doped $SU(4)$-symmetric phases. As a concrete platform, we study a bilayer triangular-lattice Hubbard model with $SU(3)$ spin symmetry and interlayer antiferromagnetic exchange. Using complementary parton constructions, we analyze doped $\mathbb{Z}_3$ quantum spin liquid and $SU(3)$-related chiral spin liquids. Doping a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ quantum spin liquid can produce an orthogonal metal with a gauge invariant fermi surface of charge-$3e$ fermionic trions. Pairing these trions gives a time-reversal-symmetric charge-$6e$ superconductor. Doping Abelian $SU(3)_1$ and $SU(6)_1$ chiral spin liquids yields chiral charge-$6e$ superconductors with and without residual Abelian topological order, respectively. Doping a non-Abelian $SU(3)_2$ chiral spin liquid leads to a non-Abelian chiral charge-$6e$ superconductor intertwined with $SO(3)_{-3}$ topological order and supporting non-Abelian $h/(6e)$ superconducting vortices. We also identify several other phases, including $\mathbb{Z}_3$ orthogonal metal, quantum anomalous Hall (crystal) phases enriched by $\mathbb{Z}_3$ or $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological order, $SU(3)$-breaking charge-$2e$ superconductors, composite fermi liquid coupled to non-Abelian gauge field, and descendant chiral spin liquids. Our results identify doped $SU(3)$ spin liquids as a natural setting where symmetry, fractionalization, and topology cooperate to produce charge-$6e$ superconductivity.
summary: This theoretical paper explores how doping SU(3) symmetric quantum spin liquids can realize exotic charge-6e superconductivity. Using advanced techniques like parton constructions on a Hubbard model, the authors demonstrate that symmetry breaking and fractionalization cooperate to stabilize these higher-charge superconducting states. It offers a powerful conceptual link between topological order in frustrated magnets and unconventional pairing mechanisms.
main_problem: The paper proposes doping SU(3)-symmetric spin liquids as a novel theoretical route to achieve exotic charge-6e superconductivity, generalizing previous work on charge-4e SC.
main_result: Doping mechanisms in SU(3) quantum spin liquids can lead to various superconducting states, including chiral and non-Abelian charge-6e superconductors by pairing fractionalized fermionic trions.
method: The study employs complementary parton constructions, mean-field ansatz calculations, and analysis of topological field theories (like Chern-Simons terms) applied to doped Hubbard models.
model_or_system: The primary model is a bilayer triangular-lattice Hubbard model possessing SU(3) spin symmetry. The theory analyzes the low-energy physics resulting from doping this system across different quantum spin liquid phases ($\mathbb{Z}_3$, Abelian/non-Abelian CSLs).
key_observables: Superconducting charge quantization (e.g., 6e), Hall conductance ($\sigma_H$), chiral central charge ($c_-$), and the nature of topological order.
important_parameters: Doping concentration ($x$), interlayer exchange coupling ($J_\perp^T$), and various symmetry-breaking parameters defining the spin liquid type (e.g., $	ext{SU}(3)_1, 	ext{SU}(3)_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on parton constructions and mean-field approximations to map out complex ground states and superconducting order parameters.
figures_summary: Figure 1 (from Chunk 4 notes) illustrates the phase diagram of an effective SU(3) spin model, showing transitions between trimer, U(1) spin liquid, and various chiral spin liquid phases as a function of temperature and coupling ratios ($K_3/J$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the physical model (Hubbard Hamiltonian with SU(3) symmetry), then using parton constructions to analyze doping effects in specific quantum spin liquids ($\mathbb{Z}_3$, CSLs), culminating in the identification of charge-6e superconducting phases.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly detailed, theoretically rigorous framework connecting higher-rank symmetries (SU(3)) and fractionalization mechanisms to predict unconventional superconductivity, which is crucial for understanding high-temperature superconductors.
